text.text: The SG-1000 was released in 1983 and was Sega's first home video game console. It was developed alongside Sega's early arcade hardware and shared similarities with other third-generation systems. The console used cartridges and Sega Cards while offering arcade-style games based on Sega's coin-operated titles. Its library included games such as Girl's Garden, Congo Bongo, Champion Baseball, and ports of Sega arcade games. The SG-1000 was followed by the SG-1000 II and later the Sega Mark III, which became the foundation for the Master System. Although it had limited success, the SG-1000 was an important step in Sega's transition into home console development.
